描述_ZN: Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains" scroll, Qing dynasty, painted by Wang Yuanqi, on paper with ink brush, 98.8 cm in length and 60.1 cm in width.　　Inscription on this scroll: "In the rainy window of the Qing Dynasty, Yu made a song of watching the long scroll of Fuchun by Dazi, and when my brother Lunxu asked for the painting on plain paper, I wrote down his intention and asked for correction, Wang Yuanqi." Inscriptions of "Wang Yuanqi Seal", "Lutai" and "Guzhi Zhai". Inscribed in the lower right corner of the "Huzhai identification" and other collection of two seals.　　The poetry hall has Chen Yuanlong, Sun Yuexuan, Hu Huien three poetry inscriptions and "Youyu leisure room treasure" and other identification Tibetan seal two parties.　　Chen Yuanlong's inscription: "The flute of a great fool went to the carriage, and the powder book was scattered and half left. The good hand now pushes Wang to give the minister, and the world sees the Fuchun picture again. Chen Yuanlong." Inscription: "Seal of Chen Yuanlong" and "Qianzhai" seal.　　Inscribed by Sun Yue: "The Fuchun Mountains are painted by Huang Gongwang, and the living face is reopened to Wang Lutai. It should be a long song that cannot be finished, and the poem in the painting shows the talent of the right minister. Sun Yue-fa." Inscriptions: "The painting of Song Shi has not yet been painted", "Seal of Sun Yue-xuan", and "Yingfeng" seal.　　The poem is inscribed by Hu Huien: "The poem is inscribed with the intention of splashing ink and strawing smoke and clouds between the feet. The book is a collection of poems by the artist. Hu Huien." Inscriptions: "Seal of Hu Huien" and "Seal of Meng Lun".　　This picture was created at the age of 52 in the 32nd year of the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing Dynasty (1693), following the brushwork of the master of Yuan Dynasty painting Huang Gongwang's masterpiece "Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains", which shows the painter's profound skills and high attainments in the management position, the opening and closing of the mountains and the use of ink and brush. Huang Gongwang in the "dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains" in the use of loose and sophisticated brushwork, Wang Yuanqi Huang Gongwang's style of painting, in the process of continuous copying formed their own style of painting. In this imitation, he is comfortable with the use of chaffing, pointing and dyeing, and his technique is superb, especially in the use of ink and brush, the first brush and then ink, staining several times, from light to thick, gradually increasing, and finally to burnt ink to break awake, giving people a sense of heaviness. Mountains and scenery are thicker, more rigorous and more detailed than those painted by Huang Gongwang. Wang Yuanqi's painting style is very distinctive among the Four Kings, and he developed Dong Qichang's pursuit of abstract ink and brush forms with programmatic features. The purpose of his paintings was to entertain the senses, with a preference for the ideal, which is significantly different from Western painting's preference for realistic scenes.
